name: Template confirmation
when: position = end of an instruction AND order = message, then FACTS, then actions, then what-happens-next AND a reference is shown if one exists — beats the Confirmation component (roles.json feedback role) because a confirmation PAGE is also the RECEIPT — that reordering is the template's whole contribution; ends a flow that template-wizard began.
$fence: EXAMPLE, NOT A PART. Dave, 14:55 2026-10-02, call 7, verbatim: "the page templates are only example or inspiration in the library for designers. automated build need to ignore these, I don't want builds to trace pages. However we probably need to create some standardised templates for some programs. They all need to be properly built. for now we have the prepped properly but we ignore them until we are working with programs to define them." So: this page is properly composed of parts (s313-D72) AND fenced — the compose door (_compose_slice.py load_graph) skips it, the generate-from-canon skill never starts from it, and _validate_example_fence.py refuses a build that reads or traces it.
purpose: The page at the end of an instruction, in two states. Confirmation is a 380px column that ENDS a flow; a confirmation PAGE has to be the RECEIPT as well, so the ORDER changes and that order is the template's whole contribution: message column, then the FACTS, then the actions, then what happens next. Actions come after the facts because a person cannot decide what to do until they have read what was done.
$provenance-note: NEW at #210 (wave 6, lane B) against the Layer-2 P3 fan-out brief - itinerary row 114. PROPOSED, NOT RULED. Layer-2 rows have no ruled artefact form; this file ships in the library's grammar on the brief's PROPOSED convention (s182-D2, the Kpi-tile precedent). No registration was performed: no CATEGORIES entry, no MIGRATED_SNIPPETS entry, no component-types.json membership, no canon.css block, no _rulings.json line, no gen_kg_edges.py run, no git operation. Deleting this pair costs nothing because nothing points at it.
$layer-note: The wave-5 and wave-6 briefs PROPOSED the meta key `layer`. meta.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with patternProperties '^\\$' only, so a bare `layer` key FAILS probe P-1 (probe_meta_schema.py). `$layer` is the legal form and is what is used here - the correction #210 wave-5 lane C reported, carried forward, not re-discovered. A `$`-prefixed key is an ANNOTATION by the schema's own grammar: if Layer-2 membership is meant to be queryable structure it wants a real enum property and a schema amendment. Still open, still Dave's.

$composes-note: REBUILT #314 lane TP (s313-D72, Dave's comment verbatim: "We need to regenerate the templates too BTW, everything in the library should be a valid 'element' of the design system"). The template is a composed PAGE: its snippet links canon/canon.css and places each part above as its own .cn-<slug> scope with the part's own markup; the page's <style> carries placement rules only (s305-D57 rule 3a; s307-D75). Before #314 it carried copies of the parts' rules and canon.css projected that second copy under its own scope. The #210 prose that stood here (which classes were copied, declaration for declaration) is retired with the copies.

accessibility.roles: No invented roles. Each specimen is a <main> whose message column is role="group" with aria-labelledby on the <h1>; each receipt is a real <dl> labelled by its panel heading; each next-steps list is an <ol>.
accessibility.keyboard: Tab order follows source order: primary action, secondary action. Two stops per page, which is the whole page.
accessibility.announcements: Neither page announces beyond its heading - the person arrived here, so the state is the destination. (Until #316 the pending page carried a role="status" chip; it was dropped with the chip, s315-D7/D33.)
accessibility.targets: ⚠ MEASURED ON THE #210 BUILD, before the #314 rebuild as a composed page; not re-measured at #314. MEASURED at 1400px: 220x44, 232x44, 304x44, 197x44. Every action clears 44px in both directions.
accessibility.$colourIsNeverAlone: The success roundel is aria-hidden and the HEADING carries the success (1.4.1). The pending roundel is aria-hidden too and the HEADING carries the pending state ('Payment waiting for approval'); the message states its consequence in prose ('Nothing has left the account yet').
accessibility.$candidateSource: ⚠ Confirmation.reference.html is itself a CANDIDATE, not gated: its meta's provenance says 'REVIEW: no Figma node yet'. Borrowing it into a template does NOT promote it, and this file must not be cited as evidence that it is settled.

antiPatterns: Giving the PENDING variant a SUCCESS device - the green roundel, the tick or the entrance pop. Pending has its own roundel since #316 (s315-D7: amber in both modes, the clock hands only); the success roundel stays for success alone.
Putting the actions before the facts. A person cannot decide what to do until they have read what was done.
Holding Confirmation's 380px at page scale. It broke 'Payment waiting for approval' after the word 'for'. The CONTAINER widens the column to 460px and asserts nothing about any molecule (s210-D3).
Animating the pending entrance. The pop is a success device.
Colouring the money. rag/*-ink is MONO ONLY and binding it here would rule on Dave's behalf.
Claiming irreversibility the product cannot honour. The success page says 'It cannot be recalled from here', which is a statement about THIS SURFACE and not about the payment scheme.

Copying a part's rules onto the page. The page places parts (its own .cn-<slug> scope + the part's own markup) and never resizes or restyles them (s305-D57 rule 3a, s307-D75). A template that re-declares a Button ladder, a Summary row or a Data-grid toolbar forks the part the moment the part moves.
